name: Victorinox Classic SD
facts: 7 functions, including a small blade, screwdriver and key ring
Small enough to live on a keychain
pitch: The gift nobody returns. It is small enough to forget about until the moment someone needs to open a package, trim a thread or tighten a screw, and then they never forget who gave it to them.

name: Olight iMini 2
pitch: A phone flashlight drains the phone. This rides on the keys and is always there for the parking lot, the dropped earbud under the car seat or the dark porch lock.

name: Nite Ize S-Biner MicroLock (2-pack)
pitch: The cheapest upgrade in EDC. It splits car keys from house keys and lets a light or a knife come off the ring in a second. Perfect stocking filler.

name: Field Notes Original Kraft (3-pack)
facts: 3.5 x 5.5 inches, fits a back pocket
pitch: For the person who still writes things down. It fits in a back pocket and has a cult following, so it reads as a thoughtful gift, not a cheap one.

name: Casio F-91W
facts: Digital sport watch with a resin strap
pitch: The most famous cheap watch in the world. It is light enough to wear to bed and cheap enough to wear to the gym, which is exactly why people end up wearing it every day.
image_alt: Casio F-91W digital watch, a budget EDC classic

name: Fisher Space Pen Bullet
facts: Pocket size when capped, full size when posted
pitch: Fisher's pressurized cartridge is made to write upside down and in the cold. Capped, it is about 3.75 inches long; with the cap posted, it is a full-size pen. It looks more expensive than it is.
image_alt: Fisher Space Pen Bullet, chrome finish

name: Gerber Dime
facts: 12 tools including pliers, a small blade and a bottle opener
pitch: Real pliers on a keychain. It is the tool people reach for at tailgates, campsites and in the junk drawer, and the bottle opener alone earns its spot.

name: SENCUT Sachse
facts: Button lock on ceramic ball bearings
pitch: A full-size folder for camping, yard work and lots of cardboard. It runs smooth on bearings and stays under $50.

name: Leatherman Skeletool CX
pitch: A full-size Leatherman that disappears in a pocket. If the person on your list already has a cheap multitool, this is the one that replaces it for good.

name: Leatherman Wave+
pitch: The multitool that ends up being handed down. It is the classic big gift for a dad, a new homeowner or anyone who fixes things. Eighteen tools, and the ones people use most open from outside without unfolding the handles.

name: Kershaw Appa
pitch: A small, all-black folder at a stocking-stuffer price. The short reverse tanto blade suits boxes, tape and zip ties, which is most of what a pocket knife actually does.

name: Gerber Pledge
pitch: Gerber's plain, practical folder for people who want a clip knife from a known brand without paying enthusiast prices.

name: Gerber Zilch
pitch: A lightweight, no-fuss folder with a full 3.1 inch blade. It is the kind of knife you hand a friend who keeps borrowing yours.

name: SENCUT ArcBlast
facts: Button lock, opens by flipper or thumb stud
pitch: A just-under-3 inch folder with a metal handle that feels solid without weighing down a pocket. The button lock makes it easy to close one handed.

name: Gerber Quadrant
pitch: A slim gentleman's folder with a bamboo handle. It looks at home with a dress shirt, which makes it an easy gift for someone who doesn't want anything tactical.

name: Buck 112 Slim Select
pitch: Buck's classic 112 shape in a light, modern build. It's a nod to the knife a lot of grandfathers carried, at about 2.5 ounces.

name: SENCUT Squiggy
facts: G10 handle with room for big hands
Button lock, flipper and thumb hole
pitch: The big one of the bunch. Pick it if you have large hands or want the most blade you can get for the money.

name: SOG Terminus XR
pitch: A sub-3 inch folder that works for left- and right-handed carry, which makes it a safe gift when you don't know which hand someone uses.

name: Kershaw Iridium
pitch: A step up from budget folders, with a clean 3.4 inch spear point blade. A good next knife for someone who has outgrown their first one.

name: Sofirn SE1
facts: Rechargeable, with UV and RGB modes
pitch: A coin-sized light for the key ring, with extra UV and colored modes. Cheap enough to buy a few as stocking stuffers.

name: Olight iUltra
pitch: Olight's newer mini keychain light. A tidy step up for someone who already likes the idea of a light on their keys.

name: Nitecore TIP3
pitch: A flat keychain light that also clips to a pocket, with a choice of warm, neutral or cool white.

name: Nitecore TINI 3
pitch: A tiny keychain light with a lot of output for its size, and a choice of light color for reading or finding things in the dark.

name: Nitecore THUMB
facts: 85 lumens white, plus a red side light
USB rechargeable, clips to keys or a cap
pitch: A tiny clip-on light whose head tilts, so it points where you need it while hanging off your keys, a bag strap or a cap brim.

name: Olight Oclip Pro
facts: Clips to a pocket, strap or collar
pitch: A light that clips on instead of riding in a pocket, so both hands stay free for dog walks, runs and car trouble.

name: Nitecore EDC09
pitch: A pocket light with a head that swivels and a magnetic tail, so it can stand on a car hood or point into an engine bay while you work.

name: Nitecore EDC29
pitch: A flat, pocketable light with huge maximum output. It's the big-gift light for someone who already owns a keychain one.

name: Olight ArkPro Ultra
pitch: Olight's premium flat EDC light. It's built to sit in a pocket like a phone, not roll around like a tube light.

name: Leatherman Rev
pitch: Leatherman's entry-level pocket tool. It has real pliers and drivers at a price that makes it an easy first Leatherman.

name: Leatherman Wingman
pitch: The value pick in Leatherman's full-size lineup. The spring-loaded pliers and scissors open on their own, which people notice the first time they use them.

name: Leatherman Rebar
pitch: A workhorse tool with replaceable wire cutters and a saw, for people who fix things more than they open packages.

name: Leatherman Signal
pitch: Leatherman's outdoor multitool, made for camping and hiking kits rather than the junk drawer.

name: Leatherman Surge
pitch: The big, heavy-duty Leatherman for work trucks, garages and the person who uses their tool every single day.

name: Casio Duro MDV106
pitch: An analog dive-style watch from Casio with 200 meter water resistance. It's a popular budget way to get the classic dive-watch look.

name: Casio G-Shock DW5600UE
pitch: The classic square G-Shock. It is built to take knocks, so it's the watch for people who work with their hands and don't want to baby a watch.
image_alt: Casio G-Shock DW-5600E square digital watch

name: Casio G-Shock GW-M5610U
pitch: The square G-Shock with solar charging and radio time sync, so it charges from light and sets its own time. The set-and-forget splurge watch.

name: Zebra F-701
pitch: An all-steel retractable pen that costs about as much as a coffee, which makes it an easy add-on to any gift.

name: Rite in the Rain No. 954 Pocket Notebook
pitch: A pocket notebook made to be written on outside, in the rain and on job sites. A small, practical stocking stuffer.
